name: Seeing, Feeling and Hearing Chinese Streets
description:
Method replication: participants rate 10 street views from five Chinese cities (the city is named under each image) with the paper's three kinds of questions: visual (building design, environment, open space: Bad / Medium / Good), emotional (beautiful, depressing, safe, lively: Low / Medium / High) and acoustic (how loud it would be: Low / Medium / High, and whether traffic, people, nature, machines or music would be heard). The images are not the paper's stimuli (90 Baidu Street View images of Shanghai, Qingdao, Chengdu, Tianjin and Xi'an, 2017–2024, cropped to remove the capture car).
Original study: Lu, Zhao, Li, Wang, Zhou & Wang (2026), "StreetSenser: a novel approach to sensing street view via a fine-tuned multimodal large language model", International Journal of Geographical Information Science 40(5), 1547–1575. 5,000 Baidu street views from various Chinese cities were split into 25 groups of 200; 100 citizens of different ages, sexes, education levels, occupations and places of residence each rated one group, and the majority answer per image became the label for fine-tuning the StreetSenser model (Qwen2.5-VL). Another 50 citizens labelled 500 validation images the same way.
Differences from the original study: (1) 10 images per participant instead of 200; (2) 90 new images from five cities instead of the paper's 5,000; (3) the sound sources are asked as Yes/No per source; (4) only age group and gender are asked about the participant.
author: Lu, Zhao, Li, Wang, Zhou & Wang
